features.name: Rage
features.desc:
In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a bonus action. While raging, you gain the following benefits if you aren't wearing heavy armor:
- You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
- When you make a melee weapon Attack using Strength, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll. This bonus increases as you level.
- You have Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
If you are able to cast Spells, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging.
Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked Unconscious or if Your Turn ends and you haven't attacked a hostile creature since your last turn or taken damage since then. You can also end your rage on Your Turn as a Bonus Action.
Once you have raged the maximum number of times for your barbarian level, you must finish a Long Rest before you can rage again. You may rage 2 times at 1st level, 3 at 3rd, 4 at 6th, 5 at 12th, and 6 at 17th.

features.name: Unarmored Defense
features.desc: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

features.name: Reckless Attack

Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

features.name: Danger Sense
features.desc: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.

features.name: Primal Path
features.desc: At 3rd level, you choose a path that shapes the nature of your rage. Choose the Path of the Berserker or the Path of the Totem Warrior, both detailed at the end of the class description. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.

features.name: Extra Attack

features.name: Fast Movement

subclasses.name: Berserker
subclasses.desc: For some barbarians, rage is a means to an end--that end being violence. The Path of the Berserker is a path of untrammeled fury, slick with blood. As you enter the berserker's rage, you thrill in the chaos of battle, heedless of your own health or well-being.

features.name: Frenzy
features.desc: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (as described in appendix A).

features.name: Mindless Rage
features.desc: Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

features.name: Intimidating Presence
features.desc:
Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.
 If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.

features.name: Retaliation
features.desc: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon Attack against that creature.

subclasses.desc: These barbarians bind themselves to a beast spirit that guides and guards them, and every rage carries some of that animal's strength, senses or instincts.

features.name: Spirit Seeker
features.desc: You can cast beast sense and speak with animals, but only as rituals: each takes 10 minutes longer than its normal casting time and needs no spell slot. Beast sense lets you touch a willing beast and share its sight and hearing for up to 1 hour (concentration), during which you are blind and deaf to your own surroundings. Speak with animals lets you understand and talk with beasts for 10 minutes. You don't otherwise know or prepare these spells.

features.name: Totem Spirit
features.desc: Pick a totem animal and gain the benefit below. You also make or find a physical totem (an amulet, charm or similar token) that includes a piece of that animal, such as fur, a feather, a claw or a tooth, and you may pick up small physical traits that recall it.

options.name: Totem Spirit: Bear
options.desc: While raging, you have resistance to every damage type except psychic.

options.name: Totem Spirit: Eagle
options.desc: While raging and not wearing heavy armor, opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage, and you can take the Dash action as a bonus action on your turn.

options.name: Totem Spirit: Wolf
options.desc: While you are raging, your allies have advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature hostile to you that is within 5 feet of you.

features.name: Aspect of the Beast
features.desc: Pick a totem animal, the same one you chose before or a different one, and gain the benefit below. These benefits work all the time, not only while raging.

options.name: Aspect of the Beast: Bear
options.desc: Your carrying capacity, including the most you can push, drag or lift, is doubled, and you have advantage on Strength checks to push, pull, lift or break objects.

options.name: Aspect of the Beast: Eagle
options.desc: You see clearly out to 1 mile, making out fine details as if they were no more than 100 feet away. Dim light doesn't give you disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks.

options.name: Aspect of the Beast: Wolf
options.desc: You can track creatures while traveling at a fast pace, and you can move stealthily while traveling at a normal pace (normally stealth needs a slow pace).

features.name: Spirit Walker
features.desc: You can cast commune with nature, but only as a ritual (10 minutes longer than its 1-minute casting time, no spell slot). It tells you up to three facts about the land within 3 miles of you (300 feet underground), such as terrain, water, plants, animals, people, powerful creatures or the influence of other planes. The answers are delivered by a spirit form of one of the animals you chose for Totem Spirit or Aspect of the Beast.

features.name: Totemic Attunement
features.desc: Pick a totem animal, whichever you chose before, and gain the benefit below.

options.name: Totemic Attunement: Bear
options.desc: While you are raging, each hostile creature within 5 feet of you has disadvantage on attack rolls against any target other than you or another creature with this feature. A creature is unaffected if it can't see or hear you or can't be frightened.

options.name: Totemic Attunement: Eagle
options.desc: While raging, you have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed. You can only fly in short bursts: if you end your turn in the air with nothing else holding you up, you fall.

options.name: Totemic Attunement: Wolf
options.desc: While raging, when you hit a Large or smaller creature with a melee weapon attack, you can use a bonus action on your turn to knock it prone.

info.name: Cantrips
info.desc: You know two cantrips of your choice from the bard spell list. You learn additional bard cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Bard table.

info.name: Spell Slots
info.desc:
The Bard table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
For example, if you know the 1st-level spell cure wounds and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast cure wounds using either slot.

info.name: Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher
info.desc:
You know four 1st-level spells of your choice from the bard spell list.
The Spells Known column of the Bard table shows when you learn more bard spells of your choice.
Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown on the table. For instance, when you reach 3rd level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the bard spells you know and replace it with another spell from the bard spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

info.name: Spellcasting Ability
info.desc:
Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your bard spells. Your magic comes from the heart and soul you pour into the performance of your music or oration. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a bard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

info.name: Ritual Casting
info.desc: You can cast any bard spell you know as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag.

info.name: Spellcasting Focus
info.desc: You can use a musical instrument (see Equipment) as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells.

features.name: Spellcasting: Bard
features.desc: You have learned to untangle and reshape the fabric of reality in harmony with your wishes and music. Your spells are part of your vast repertoire, magic that you can tune to different situations.

features.name: Bardic Inspiration (d6)
features.desc:
You can inspire others through stirring words or music. To do so, you use a bonus action on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die, a d6. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the d20 before deciding to use the Bardic Inspiration die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the Bardic Inspiration die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest. 
Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level.

The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

subclasses.name: Lore
subclasses.desc: Bards of the College of Lore know something about most things, collecting bits of knowledge from sources as diverse as scholarly tomes and peasant tales. Whether singing folk ballads in taverns or elaborate compositions in royal courts, these bards use their gifts to hold audiences spellbound. When the applause dies down, the audience members might find themselves questioning everything they held to be true, from their faith in the priesthood of the local temple to their loyalty to the king. The loyalty of these bards lies in the pursuit of beauty and truth, not in fealty to a monarch or following the tenets of a deity. A noble who keeps such a bard as a herald or advisor knows that the bard would rather be honest than politic. The college's members gather in libraries and sometimes in actual colleges, complete with classrooms and dormitories, to share their lore with one another. They also meet at festivals or affairs of state, where they can expose corruption, unravel lies, and poke fun at self-important figures of authority.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.desc: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: Cutting Words
features.desc:
Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others.
When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll.
You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the GM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature is immune if it can't hear you or if it's immune to being charmed.

features.name: Additional Magical Secrets
features.desc: At 6th level, you learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don't count against the number of bard spells you know.

features.name: Peerless Skill
features.desc: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check, but before the GM tells you whether you succeed or fail.

subclasses.name: Valor
subclasses.desc: Bards of Valor are battlefield skalds who fight beside heroes, keep their deeds alive in song and spur their companions to match them.

features.name: Combat Inspiration

Right after rolling damage for a weapon attack, it can roll the die and add the result to that damage. Or, when an attack roll is made against it, it can use its reaction to roll the die and add the result to its AC against that one attack, deciding after the attack is rolled but before knowing whether it hits.

info.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
info.desc:
The Cleric table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
You prepare the list of cleric spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the cleric spell list. When you do so, choose a number of cleric spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your cleric level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
For example, if you are a 3rd-level cleric, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. subclasses.name: Life
subclasses.desc: The Life domain focuses on the vibrant positive energy--one of the fundamental forces of the universe--that sustains all life. The gods of life promote vitality and health through healing the sick and wounded, caring for those in need, and driving away the forces of death and undeath. Almost any non-evil deity can claim influence over this domain, particularly agricultural deities, sun gods, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.desc: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Disciple of Life
features.desc: Also starting at 1st level, your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to heal the badly injured.
As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy that can restore a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level.
Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide those hit points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can't use this feature on an undead or a construct.

features.name: Blessed Healer
features.desc: Beginning at 6th level, the healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.desc: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Supreme Healing
features.desc: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12.

subclasses.name: Knowledge
subclasses.desc: Clerics of knowledge gods chase lore and hidden truths, guard libraries and secrets alike, and can draw thoughts straight out of other minds.

features.name: Blessings of Knowledge: Languages
features.desc: You learn two languages of your choice.

features.name: Blessings of Knowledge: Skills
features.desc: Choose two of Arcana, History, Nature and Religion. You become proficient in both, and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with either of them.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
features.desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity and choose one skill or tool. You are proficient with it for the next 10 minutes.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
features.desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity and choose a creature you can see within 60 feet. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a success, you can't use this feature on it again until you finish a long rest. On a failure, for 1 minute you can read its surface thoughts (its current feelings and what it is actively thinking about) while it is within 60 feet of you. During that minute you can use your action to end the effect and cast suggestion on the creature without expending a spell slot; it automatically fails its saving throw against that suggestion.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
features.desc: Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Visions of the Past
features.desc:
You can meditate and pray for at least 1 minute to see hazy, dreamlike visions of recent events tied to an object you hold or to the place around you. You can keep meditating for up to a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score, concentrating as if on a spell. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Object reading: holding an object, after 1 minute you learn how its previous owner came to have it and lost it, and the most recent significant event involving the object and that owner. If other creatures owned it within a number of days equal to your Wisdom score, each extra minute reveals the same for one more of those owners.
Area reading: you see recent events in your immediate surroundings (a room, street, tunnel, clearing or similar space, up to a 50-foot cube), going back a number of days equal to your Wisdom score. Each minute of meditation reveals one significant event, most recent first: usually an emotionally charged moment such as violence, treachery, a celebration or a death, or an everyday happening that matters to your current situation.

subclasses.name: Light
subclasses.desc: Clerics of light serve gods of the sun, fire and truth, burning away darkness and deceit with radiant power.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
features.desc: You learn the light cantrip if you don't already know it. It doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

features.name: Warding Flare
features.desc: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you attacks you, you can use your reaction to flash bright light in its eyes before the attack hits or misses, giving the attack roll disadvantage. Creatures that can't be blinded are immune. You can use this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) and regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
features.desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity and present your holy symbol. All magical darkness within 30 feet of you is dispelled, and each hostile creature within 30 feet makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 2d10 + your cleric level radiant damage on a failure, or half as much on a success. Creatures with total cover from you are unaffected.

features.name: Improved Flare
features.desc: You can also use Warding Flare when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you attacks a creature other than you.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
features.desc: Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Corona of Light
features.desc: As an action, wrap yourself in an aura of sunlight for 1 minute, or until you end it with another action. You shed bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light for another 30 feet beyond that. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any spell that deals fire or radiant damage.

subclasses.name: Nature
subclasses.desc: Clerics of nature gods tend the wild places, speak for beasts and growing things, and turn the elements against those who would harm them.

features.name: Acolyte of Nature: Cantrip
features.desc: You learn one cantrip of your choice from the druid spell list, on top of your usual cantrips. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

features.name: Acolyte of Nature: Skill
features.desc: You become proficient in one of these skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Nature or Survival.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
features.desc: You become proficient with heavy armor.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
features.desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity, present your holy symbol and call on your deity. Each beast or plant creature within 30 feet of you that can see you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it is charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes damage, and while charmed it is friendly to you and to any creatures you name.

features.name: Dampen Elements
features.desc: When you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to give that creature resistance to that instance of the damage.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.desc: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 cold, fire or lightning damage (your choice) to it. At 14th level the extra damage becomes 2d8.

features.name: Master of Nature
features.desc: While creatures are charmed by your Charm Animals and Plants, you can use a bonus action on your turn to tell each of them aloud what it will do on its next turn.

subclasses.name: Tempest
subclasses.desc: Tempest clerics serve gods of storm, sea and sky, and answer their enemies with thunder, lightning and screaming wind.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.desc: You become proficient with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: Wrath of the Storm
features.desc: When a creature you can see within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to make it attempt a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. It takes 2d8 lightning or thunder damage (your choice) on a failure, or half as much on a success. You can use this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) and regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath
features.desc: When you roll lightning or thunder damage, you can spend one use of Channel Divinity to deal the maximum possible damage instead of rolling.

features.name: Thunderbolt Strike
features.desc: When you deal lightning damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 feet away from you.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.desc: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 thunder damage to it. At 14th level the extra damage becomes 2d8.

features.name: Stormborn
features.desc: Whenever you are not underground or indoors, you have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed.

subclasses.name: Trickery
subclasses.desc: Clerics of trickster gods spread mischief and confusion, slipping past the powerful with illusions, disguises and borrowed faces.

features.name: Blessing of the Trickster
features.desc: As an action, touch a willing creature other than yourself. It has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks for 1 hour, or until you use this feature again.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
features.desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity to create a flawless illusion of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. It lasts 1 minute, or until you lose concentration (as if concentrating on a spell). As a bonus action on your turn, you can move it up to 30 feet to a space you can see, but it must stay within 120 feet of you. While it lasts, you can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, but you still use your own senses. When both you and the illusion are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
features.desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity to become invisible until the end of your next turn. You become visible if you attack or cast a spell.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.desc: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 poison damage to it. At 14th level the extra damage becomes 2d8.

features.name: Improved Duplicity
features.desc: Invoke Duplicity now creates up to four illusions of you instead of one. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move any number of them up to 30 feet each, keeping them within 120 feet of you.

subclasses.name: War
subclasses.desc: War clerics serve gods of battle and courage, fighting on the front line and guiding their companions' blows home.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.desc: You become proficient with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: War Priest
features.desc: When you take the Attack action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) and regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
features.desc: When you make an attack roll, you can spend one use of Channel Divinity to add +10 to it. You decide after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

features.name: Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing
features.desc: When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction and one use of Channel Divinity to give it +10 on that roll. You decide after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

features.desc: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 damage of the same type the weapon deals. At 14th level the extra damage becomes 2d8.

features.name: Avatar of Battle
features.desc: You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.

You and others who know this language automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check but can't decipher it without magic.

features.name: Wild Shape (CR 1/4 or below, no flying or swim speed)
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your action to magically assume the shape of a beast that you have seen before. You can use this feature twice. You regain expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.
Your druid level determines the beasts you can transform into, as shown in the Beast Shapes table. At 2nd level, for example, you can transform into any beast that has a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower that doesn't have a flying or swimming speed.

You can revert to your normal form earlier by using a bonus action on your turn. You automatically revert if you fall unconscious, drop to 0 hit points, or die.
While you are transformed, the following rules apply:

You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. If the creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block is higher than yours, use the creature's bonus instead of yours. If the creature has any legendary or lair actions, you can't use them.

For example, if you take 10 damage in animal form and have only 1 hit point left, you revert and take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren't knocked unconscious.

Transforming doesn't break your concentration on a spell you've already cast, however, or prevent you from taking actions that are part of a spell, such as call lightning, that you've already cast.

- You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the GM decides whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature's shape and size. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.

These druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of communities that hold to the Old Faith and serve as advisors to the rulers of those folk. As a member of this circle, your magic is influenced by the land where you were initiated into the circle's mysterious rites.

features.name: Circle Spells: your land
features.desc: Your circle is bound to one kind of land. It decides the circle spells you always have prepared at 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th level.

options.name: Land: Arctic
options.desc: Your magic is rooted in frozen plains, glaciers and tundra.

options.name: Land: Coast

options.name: Land: Desert

options.name: Land: Forest

options.name: Land: Grassland

options.name: Land: Mountain

options.name: Land: Swamp

options.name: Land: Underdark
options.desc: Your magic is rooted in the caverns and tunnels far below the surface.

features.name: Natural Recovery

The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Land's Stride

features.name: Nature's Ward
features.desc: When you reach 10th level, you can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.

features.name: Nature's Sanctuary

When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours. features.name: Combat Wild Shape

features.name: Circle Forms
features.desc: Your Wild Shape can turn you into a beast with a challenge rating as high as 1, ignoring the Max. CR column of the Beast Shapes table. Its other limits still apply: no swimming speed before 4th level and no flying speed before 8th. From 6th level, the highest challenge rating you can take is your druid level divided by 3, rounded down.

features.name: Primal Strike
features.desc: Your attacks in beast form count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

features.name: Elemental Wild Shape
features.desc: You can spend two uses of Wild Shape at once to transform into an air elemental, earth elemental, fire elemental or water elemental.

features.name: Thousand Forms
features.desc: You can cast alter self at will, without expending a spell slot.

subclasses.desc: A student of tactics who reads every fight like a puzzle, spending bursts of drilled technique to trip, disarm, shove and outmanoeuvre the enemy while steering allies into the right place.

features.name: Combat Superiority
features.desc: You learn three maneuvers of your choice and gain four superiority dice, which are d8s. Using a maneuver spends one superiority die, with no more than one maneuver per attack. options.desc: When you take the Attack action, give up one of your attacks and use your bonus action to spend a superiority die. A friendly creature that can see or hear you may immediately use its reaction to make one weapon attack, adding the die to its damage roll.

options.desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. The target makes a Strength save against your maneuver save DC; on a failure it drops one item of your choice that it is holding, which lands at its feet.

options.name: Maneuver: Distracting Strike
options.desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. The next attack roll against that target by anyone other than you has advantage, as long as it is made before the start of your next turn.

options.name: Maneuver: Evasive Footwork
options.desc: As you move, you can spend a superiority die: roll it and add the result to your AC for the rest of that movement.

options.desc: As a bonus action on your turn, spend a superiority die to feint at one creature within 5 feet of you. You have advantage on your next attack roll against it this turn, and if that attack hits, add the die to the damage.

options.desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. The target makes a Wisdom save against your maneuver save DC; on a failure it has disadvantage on attack rolls against anyone other than you until the end of your next turn.

options.name: Maneuver: Lunging Attack
options.desc: When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn, spend a superiority die to give that attack 5 extra feet of reach. On a hit, add the die to the damage.

options.desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. Choose a friendly creature that can see or hear you: it can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks from your target.

options.name: Maneuver: Menacing Attack

options.name: Maneuver: Parry
options.desc: If a creature's melee attack deals you damage, you can react by spending a superiority die: the damage drops by the die roll + your Dexterity modifier.

options.name: Maneuver: Precision Attack
options.desc: When you make a weapon attack roll against a creature, spend a superiority die and add it to the attack roll. You can decide before or after rolling, but before the attack's effects are applied.

options.desc: If a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can react by spending a superiority die to strike back with a melee weapon attack; on a hit, the die is added to the damage.

subclasses.name: Eldritch Knight
subclasses.desc: A warrior who studies wizardry to guard and sharpen their swordwork, weaving wards and bursts of force between blows and calling a bonded weapon back to hand at will.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.desc: You learn wizard spells and cast them with Intelligence: your spell save DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier, and your spell attack modifier is your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. You know two wizard cantrips of your choice, and a third at 10th level. At 3rd level you know three 1st-level wizard spells, two of which must be abjuration or evocation. Every spell you learn later must also be abjuration or evocation, except the ones you learn at 8th, 14th and 20th level, which can come from any school; each must be of a level you have spell slots for (your slots follow the Eldritch Knight third-caster table, reaching 4th-level spells at 19th level). You don't prepare spells: you cast the ones you know. Whenever you gain a fighter level, you may replace one wizard spell you know with another of a level you have slots for, which must be abjuration or evocation unless it replaces one of your any-school spells.

features.name: Weapon Bond
features.desc: Through a 1-hour ritual (which you can perform during a short rest), with the weapon within your reach the whole time, you bond yourself to a weapon you touch. While bonded, you can't be disarmed of it unless you are incapacitated, and if it is on the same plane of existence as you, you can use a bonus action on your turn to make it teleport instantly into your hand. You can have up to two bonded weapons but summon only one per bonus action; to bond a third, you must first break the bond with one of the other two.

features.name: War Magic
features.desc: Casting a cantrip with your action lets you make one weapon attack as a bonus action that turn.

features.name: Eldritch Strike
features.desc: A creature you hit with a weapon attack is left open to your magic: until the end of your next turn, it makes its next saving throw against one of your spells with disadvantage.

features.name: Arcane Charge
features.desc: When you use Action Surge, you can also teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, either before or after the extra action.

features.name: Improved War Magic
features.desc: Casting any spell with your action, cantrip or leveled, lets you make one weapon attack as a bonus action that turn.

toolChoices.desc: Choose one type of artisan's tools or one musical instrument

equipmentOptions.desc: (a) a shortsword or (b) any simple weapon

features.name: Unarmored Defense
features.desc: Beginning at 1st level, while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

features.name: Martial Arts
features.desc:
At 1st level, your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and monk weapons, which are shortswords and any simple melee weapons that don't have the two- handed or heavy property.
You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a shield:
- You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and monk weapons.
- You can roll a d4 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or monk weapon. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of Table: The Monk.
- When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a monk weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and attack with a quarterstaff, you can also make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, assuming you haven't already taken a bonus action this turn.
Certain monasteries use specialized forms of the monk weapons. For example, you might use a club that is two lengths of wood connected by a short chain (called a nunchaku) or a sickle with a shorter, straighter blade (called a kama). Whatever name you use for a monk weapon, you can use the game statistics provided for the weapon.

features.name: Ki
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, your training allows you to harness the mystic energy of ki. Your access to this energy is represented by a number of ki points. Your monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Ki Points column of Table: The Monk.
You can spend these points to fuel various ki features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more ki features as you gain levels in this class.
When you spend a ki point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you draw all of your expended ki back into yourself. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your ki points.
Some of your ki features require your target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Ki save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

features.name: Flurry of Blows
features.desc: Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.

features.name: Patient Defense
features.desc: You can spend 1 ki point to take the Dodge action as a bonus action on your turn.

features.name: Step of the Wind
features.desc: You can spend 1 ki point to take the Disengage or Dash action as a bonus action on your turn, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

features.name: Unarmored Movement
features.desc:
Starting at 2nd level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain monk levels, as shown in Table: The Monk.
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.

features.name: Monastic Tradition
features.desc: When you reach 3rd level, you commit yourself to a monastic tradition, such as the Way of the Open Hand. Your tradition grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

features.name: Deflect Missiles
features.desc:
Starting at 3rd level, you can use your reaction to deflect or catch the missile when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level.
If you reduce the damage to 0, you can catch the missile if it is small enough for you to hold in one hand and you have at least one hand free. If you catch a missile in this way, you can spend 1 ki point to make a ranged attack with the weapon or piece of ammunition you just caught, as part of the same reaction. You make this attack with proficiency, regardless of your weapon proficiencies, and the missile counts as a monk weapon for the attack, which has a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

features.name: Slow Fall
features.desc: Beginning at 4th level, you can use your reaction when you fall to reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to five times your monk level.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Stunning Strike
features.desc: Starting at 5th level, you can interfere with the flow of ki in an opponent's body. When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Ki Empowered Strikes
features.desc: Starting at 6th level, your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

features.name: Monastic Tradition feature
features.desc: When you reach 3rd level, you commit yourself to a monastic tradition, such as the Way of the Open Hand. Your tradition grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

features.name: Evasion
features.desc: At 7th level, your instinctive agility lets you dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a blue dragon's lightning breath or a fireball spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

features.name: Stillness of Mind
features.desc: Starting at 7th level, you can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

features.name: Purity of Body
features.desc: At 10th level, your mastery of the ki flowing through you makes you immune to disease and poison.

features.name: Tongue of the Sun and Moon
features.desc: Starting at 13th level, you learn to touch the ki of other minds so that you understand all spoken languages. Moreover, any creature that can understand a language can understand what you say.

features.name: Diamond Soul
features.desc:
Beginning at 14th level, your mastery of ki grants you proficiency in all saving throws.
Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can spend 1 ki point to reroll it and take the second result.

features.name: Timeless Body
features.desc: At 15th level, your ki sustains you so that you suffer none of the frailty of old age, and you can't be aged magically. You can still die of old age, however. In addition, you no longer need food or water.

features.desc: When you reach 3rd level, you commit yourself to a monastic tradition, such as the Way of the Open Hand. Your tradition grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

features.name: Empty Body
features.desc:
Beginning at 18th level, you can use your action to spend 4 ki points to become invisible for 1 minute. During that time, you also have resistance to all damage but force damage.
Additionally, you can spend 8 ki points to cast the astral projection spell, without needing material components. When you do so, you can't take any other creatures with you.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

features.name: Perfect Self
features.desc: At 20th level, when you roll for initiative and have no ki points remaining, you regain 4 ki points.

subclasses.name: Open Hand
subclasses.desc: Monks of the Way of the Open Hand are the ultimate masters of martial arts combat, whether armed or unarmed. They learn techniques to push and trip their opponents, manipulate ki to heal damage to their bodies, and practice advanced meditation that can protect them from harm.

features.name: Open Hand Technique
features.desc:
Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can manipulate your enemy's ki when you harness your own. Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target:
- It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
- It must make a Strength saving throw. If it fails, you can push it up to 15 feet away from you.
- It can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Wholeness of Body
features.desc: At 6th level, you gain the ability to heal yourself. As an action, you can regain hit points equal to three times your monk level. You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.

features.name: Tranquility
features.desc: Beginning at 11th level, you can enter a special meditation that surrounds you with an aura of peace. At the end of a long rest, you gain the effect of a sanctuary spell that lasts until the start of your next long rest (the spell can end early as normal). The saving throw DC for the spell equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your proficiency bonus.

features.name: Quivering Palm
features.desc:
At 17th level, you gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you use your action to end them. To do so, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. When you use this action, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, it is reduced to 0 hit points. If it succeeds, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage.
You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time. You can choose to end the vibrations harmlessly without using an action.

subclasses.name: Shadow
subclasses.desc: Monks of a quiet, secretive order who train in stealth and silence, wrapping themselves in darkness to strike unseen and vanish before the alarm is raised.

features.name: Shadow Arts
features.desc: As an action, you can spend 2 ki points to cast darkness, darkvision, pass without trace or silence, without needing material components. These spells otherwise follow their normal rules, including concentration. You also know the minor illusion cantrip (nothing changes if you already knew it).

features.name: Shadow Step
features.desc: As a bonus action while you stand in dim light or darkness, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also dimly lit or dark. Your first melee attack before the turn ends has advantage.

features.name: Cloak of Shadows
features.desc: In dim light or darkness, you can spend your action to turn invisible. The invisibility ends as soon as you attack, cast a spell, or are in bright light.

features.name: Opportunist
features.desc: If someone other than you hits a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against that creature.

subclasses.name: Four Elements
subclasses.desc: Monks who bend their ki into the raw forces of air, earth, fire and water, hurling flame from their fists, shaping ice and riding the wind.

features.name: Discipline: Elemental Attunement
features.desc: No ki cost. As an action, you briefly command the elements nearby to do one of these: make a harmless, instantaneous sensory effect of air, earth, fire or water (a spray of sparks, a puff of breeze, a fine mist, a low rumble of stone); instantly light or put out a candle, torch or small campfire; chill or warm up to 1 pound of nonliving material for up to 1 hour; or make earth, fire, water or mist that fits in a 1-foot cube hold a crude shape you choose for 1 minute.

features.name: Disciple of the Elements
features.desc: You learn elemental disciplines, techniques powered by ki. Every monk of this tradition knows Elemental Attunement; pick one other discipline here. You learn one more discipline at 6th, 11th and 17th level, and whenever you learn one you may also swap a discipline you know for another. Disciplines that copy a spell use that spell's casting time and normal rules but need no material components, and any saving throw uses your ki save DC (8 + proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier). If such a spell gets stronger when cast at a higher level, you can spend extra ki to raise its level by one per extra ki point. The most ki you can spend on one discipline, base cost included, depends on your monk level: 2 at 3rd-4th, 3 at 5th-8th, 4 at 9th-12th, 5 at 13th-16th, and 6 at 17th-20th.

options.name: Discipline: Breath of Winter
options.desc: Spend 6 ki points to cast cone of cold: each creature in a 60-foot cone from you makes a Constitution save, taking 8d8 cold damage on a failure or half on a success. A creature it kills is left a frozen statue.

options.name: Discipline: Clench of the North Wind
options.desc: Spend 3 ki points to cast hold person: a humanoid you can see within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save or is paralyzed for up to 1 minute (concentration), repeating the save at the end of each of its turns. Each extra ki point (up to your maximum) raises the spell level by one and adds a target.

options.name: Discipline: Eternal Mountain Defense
options.desc: Spend 5 ki points to cast stoneskin on yourself: you have resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage for up to 1 hour (concentration).

options.name: Discipline: Fangs of the Fire Snake
options.desc: When you take the Attack action on your turn, spend 1 ki point to wreathe your fists and feet in lashing flame: for that action and the rest of the turn your unarmed strikes gain 10 feet of reach and deal fire damage instead of bludgeoning. When one of these strikes hits, you can spend 1 more ki point to add 1d10 fire damage.

options.name: Discipline: Fist of Four Thunders
options.desc: Spend 2 ki points to cast thunderwave: each creature in a 15-foot cube starting from you makes a Constitution save, taking 2d8 thunder damage and being pushed 10 feet away on a failure, or half damage and no push on a success. Unsecured objects in the area are pushed too, and the boom is audible 300 feet away. Each extra ki point (up to your maximum) raises the spell level by one for +1d8 damage.

options.name: Discipline: Fist of Unbroken Air
options.desc: As an action, spend 2 ki points and pick a creature within 30 feet of you. It makes a Strength save. On a failure it takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage, plus 1d10 for each extra ki point you spend (up to your maximum), and you can push it up to 20 feet away from you and knock it prone. On a success it takes half damage and is neither pushed nor knocked prone.

options.name: Discipline: Flames of the Phoenix
options.desc: Spend 4 ki points to cast fireball: a 20-foot-radius burst at a point you choose within 150 feet. Each creature in it makes a Dexterity save, taking 8d6 fire damage on a failure or half on a success, and unattended flammable objects catch fire. Each extra ki point (up to your maximum) raises the spell level by one for +1d6 damage.

options.name: Discipline: Gong of the Summit
options.desc: Spend 3 ki points to cast shatter: a ringing blast fills a 10-foot-radius sphere at a point within 60 feet. Each creature in it makes a Constitution save, taking 3d8 thunder damage on a failure or half on a success; creatures of stone, crystal or metal save with disadvantage, and unattended nonmagical objects there take the damage too. Each extra ki point (up to your maximum) raises the spell level by one for +1d8 damage.

options.name: Discipline: Mist Stance
options.desc: Spend 4 ki points to cast gaseous form on yourself: for up to 1 hour (concentration) you become a drifting cloud with a 10-foot flying speed. You can slip through tiny cracks and enter other creatures' spaces, have resistance to nonmagical damage and advantage on Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saves, but you can't talk, handle objects, attack or cast spells.

options.name: Discipline: Ride the Wind
options.desc: Spend 4 ki points to cast fly on yourself: you gain a flying speed of 60 feet for up to 10 minutes (concentration). If it ends while you are aloft, you fall.

options.name: Discipline: River of Hungry Flame
options.desc: Spend 5 ki points to cast wall of fire: an opaque wall of flame within 120 feet, either straight (up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, 1 foot thick) or a ring (up to 20 feet across, 20 feet high), lasting up to 1 minute (concentration). Creatures in its space when it appears make a Dexterity save, taking 5d8 fire damage or half on a success. One side of your choice burns: a creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of that side or inside the wall takes 5d8 fire damage, as does a creature entering the wall for the first time on a turn. An extra ki point (if your maximum allows) raises the spell level for +1d8 damage.

options.name: Discipline: Rush of the Gale Spirits
options.desc: Spend 2 ki points to cast gust of wind: a line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide blasts from you for up to 1 minute (concentration). A creature that starts its turn in the line makes a Strength save or is pushed 15 feet away from you along it, and moving toward you through it costs double movement. It scatters gas and fog and snuffs out candles, torches and other unprotected flames. As a bonus action on later turns you can change the line's direction.

options.name: Discipline: Shape the Flowing River
options.desc: As an action, spend 1 ki point and choose an area of water or ice no more than 30 feet on a side within 120 feet of you. info.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
info.desc:
The Paladin table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells. To cast one of your paladin spells of 1st level or higher, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
You prepare the list of paladin spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the paladin spell list. When you do so, choose a number of paladin spells equal to your Charisma modifier + half your paladin level, rounded down (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
For example, if you are a 5th-level paladin, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With a Charisma of 14, your list of prepared spells can include four spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination. If you prepare the 1st-level spell cure wounds, you can cast it using a 1st-level or a 2nd- level slot. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells.
You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of paladin spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

info.name: Spellcasting Ability
info.desc:
Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your paladin spells, since their power derives from the strength of your convictions. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a paladin spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

info.name: Spellcasting Focus
info.desc: You can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus for your paladin spells.

features.name: Divine Sense
features.desc:
The presence of strong evil registers on your senses like a noxious odor, and powerful good rings like heavenly music in your ears. As an action, you can open your awareness to detect such forces. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any celestial, fiend, or undead within 60 feet of you that is not behind total cover. You know the type (celestial, fiend, or undead) of any being whose presence you sense, but not its identity. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the hallow spell.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier. When you finish a long rest, you regain all expended uses.

features.name: Lay on Hands
features.desc:
Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you take a long rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of hit points equal to your paladin level x 5.
As an action, you can touch a creature and draw power from the pool to restore a number of hit points to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in your pool.
Alternatively, you can expend 5 hit points from your pool of healing to cure the target of one disease or neutralize one poison affecting it. You can cure multiple diseases and neutralize multiple poisons with a single use of Lay on Hands, expending hit points separately for each one.
This feature has no effect on undead and constructs.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.desc: At 2nd level, you adopt a style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

options.name: Fighting Style: Defense
options.desc: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

options.name: Fighting Style: Dueling
options.desc: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

options.name: Fighting Style: Great Weapon Fighting
options.desc: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

options.name: Fighting Style: Protection
options.desc: When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.

features.name: Spellcasting: Paladin
features.desc: By 2nd level, you have learned to draw on divine magic through meditation and prayer to cast spells as a cleric does.

features.name: Divine Smite
features.desc: Starting at 2nd level, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st, to a maximum of 5d8. The damage increases by 1d8 if the target is an undead or a fiend.

features.name: Divine Health
features.desc: By 3rd level, the divine magic flowing through you makes you immune to disease.

features.name: Sacred Oath
features.desc:
When you reach 3rd level, you swear the oath that binds you as a paladin forever. Up to this time you have been in a preparatory stage, committed to the path but not yet sworn to it. Now you choose an oath, such as the Oath of Devotion.
Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 15th, and 20th level. Those features include oath spells and the Channel Divinity feature.

features.name: Oath Spells
features.desc:
Each oath has a list of associated spells. You gain access to these spells at the levels specified in the oath description. Once you gain access to an oath spell, you always have it prepared. Oath spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.
If you gain an oath spell that doesn't appear on the paladin spell list, the spell is nonetheless a paladin spell for you.

features.name: Channel Divinity
features.desc:
Your oath allows you to channel divine energy to fuel magical effects. Each Channel Divinity option provided by your oath explains how to use it.
When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which option to use. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Channel Divinity again.
Some Channel Divinity effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your paladin spell save DC.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.desc: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Aura of Protection
features.desc:
Starting at 6th level, whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you must make a saving throw, the creature gains a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Charisma modifier (with a minimum bonus of +1). You must be conscious to grant this bonus.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

features.name: Sacred Oath feature
features.desc:
When you reach 3rd level, you swear the oath that binds you as a paladin forever. Up to this time you have been in a preparatory stage, committed to the path but not yet sworn to it. Now you choose an oath, such as the Oath of Devotion.
Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 15th, and 20th level. Those features include oath spells and the Channel Divinity feature.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

features.name: Aura of Courage
features.desc:
Starting at 10th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be frightened while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

features.name: Improved Divine Smite
features.desc: By 11th level, you are so suffused with righteous might that all your melee weapon strikes carry divine power with them. Whenever you hit a creature with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 1d8 radiant damage. If you also use your Divine Smite with an attack, you add this damage to the extra damage of your Divine Smite.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

features.name: Cleansing Touch
features.desc:
Beginning at 14th level, you can use your action to end one spell on yourself or on one willing creature that you touch.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Devotion
subclasses.desc: The Oath of Devotion binds a paladin to the loftiest ideals of justice, virtue, and order. Sometimes called cavaliers, white knights, or holy warriors, these paladins meet the ideal of the knight in shining armor, acting with honor in pursuit of justice and the greater good. They hold themselves to the highest standards of conduct, and some, for better or worse, hold the rest of the world to the same standards. Many who swear this oath are devoted to gods of law and good and use their gods' tenets as the measure of their devotion. They hold angels--the perfect servants of good--as their ideals, and incorporate images of angelic wings into their helmets or coats of arms.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Sacred Weapon
features.desc:
As an action, you can imbue one weapon that you are holding with positive energy, using your Channel Divinity. For 1 minute, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls made with that weapon (with a minimum bonus of +1). The weapon also emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light 20 feet beyond that. If the weapon is not already magical, it becomes magical for the duration.
You can end this effect on your turn as part of any other action. If you are no longer holding or carrying this weapon, or if you fall unconscious, this effect ends.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Turn the Unholy
features.desc:
As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring fiends and undead, using your Channel Divinity. Each fiend or undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.
A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.

features.name: Aura of Devotion
features.desc:
Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

features.name: Purity of Spirit
features.desc: Beginning at 15th level, you are always under the effects of a protection from evil and good spell.

features.name: Holy Nimbus
features.desc:
At 20th level, as an action, you can emanate an aura of sunlight. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that.
Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage.
In addition, for the duration, you have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead.

subclasses.name: Ancients
subclasses.desc: Paladins sworn to protect light, life and beauty against everything that would wither them, often marked by leaves, antlers or blossoms worked into their armour.

features.name: Tenets of the Ancients
features.desc: Kindle the Light: spread hope through mercy, kindness and forgiveness. Shelter the Light: stand guard over goodness, beauty, love and laughter, and over every place where life flourishes. Preserve Your Own Light: keep your own joy alive through song, art and delight, or you will have none left to share. Be the Light: let your courage and gladness be a beacon to everyone lost in despair.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Nature's Wrath
features.desc: As an action, spend your Channel Divinity to make spectral vines lunge at a creature you can see within 10 feet of you. It makes a Strength or Dexterity save (its choice) against your spell save DC or is restrained. While restrained, it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns; on a success it breaks free and the vines vanish.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Turn the Faithless
features.desc: As an action, present your holy symbol and spend your Channel Divinity. Each fey and fiend within 30 feet of you that can hear you makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC. On a failure it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage: it must spend its turns moving as far from you as it can, can't willingly move within 30 feet of you, can't take reactions, and for its action can only Dash or try to escape something stopping it from moving (or Dodge if it has nowhere to go). While turned, a creature hiding its true form behind an illusion, shapechange or similar effect is revealed.

features.name: Aura of Warding
features.desc: You and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you take half damage from spells (resistance to spell damage). From 18th level the aura extends to 30 feet.

features.name: Undying Sentinel
features.desc: Once per long rest, if something would drop you to 0 hit points without killing you outright, you can stay standing at 1 hit point instead. In addition, old age no longer weakens you, and magic can't age you.

features.name: Elder Champion
features.desc: As an action, take on the form of an ancient force of nature (you choose its look) for 1 minute. While transformed: you regain 10 hit points at the start of each of your turns; you can cast a paladin spell with a casting time of 1 action as a bonus action instead; and enemy creatures within 10 feet of you have disadvantage on saving throws against your paladin spells and Channel Divinity options. Once used, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Vengeance
subclasses.desc: Paladins sworn to hunt down those who commit great wrongs, setting aside mercy and their own comfort until the guilty are brought low.

features.name: Tenets of Vengeance
features.desc: Fight the Greater Evil: when you must choose, go after the worse evil rather than the lesser one. No Mercy for the Wicked: ordinary foes may earn your mercy, but your sworn enemies never do. By Any Means Necessary: don't let your scruples stop you from destroying your foes. Restitution: when your foes ruin lives, you share the blame for not stopping them, so you help the people they have harmed.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Abjure Enemy
features.desc: As an action, present your holy symbol and spend your Channel Divinity to denounce one creature you can see within 60 feet. Unless it is immune to being frightened, it makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC (fiends and undead have disadvantage). On a failure it is frightened for 1 minute or until it takes any damage, and while frightened its speed is 0 and can't be increased. On a success its speed is halved for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Vow of Enmity
features.desc: Use a bonus action and your Channel Divinity to swear vengeance on a creature you can see within 10 feet. For 1 minute, or until it drops to 0 hit points or falls unconscious, your attack rolls against it have advantage.

features.name: Relentless Avenger
features.desc: Landing an opportunity attack lets you give chase: as part of that same reaction, you can move up to half your speed right away, and this movement provokes no opportunity attacks.

features.name: Soul of Vengeance
features.desc: Whenever the target of your Vow of Enmity makes an attack, you can answer with your reaction: one melee weapon attack against it, if it is within your reach.

features.name: Avenging Angel
features.desc: As an action, transform for 1 hour: wings grow from your back, giving you a flying speed of 60 feet, and you radiate a menacing aura in a 30-foot radius. The first time an enemy enters the aura or starts its turn in it during a battle, it makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC or is frightened of you for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. Attack rolls against a creature frightened this way have advantage. Once used, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
