info.name: Spell Slots
info.desc:
The Ranger table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
For example, if you know the 1st-level spell animal friendship and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast animal friendship using either slot.

info.name: Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher
info.desc:
You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the ranger spell list.
The Spells Known column of the Ranger table shows when you learn more ranger spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 5th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the ranger spells you know and replace it with another spell from the ranger spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

info.name: Spellcasting Ability
info.desc:
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your ranger spells, since your magic draws on your attunement to nature. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a ranger spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

features.name: Favored Enemy (1 type)
features.desc:
Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, hunting, and even talking to a certain type of enemy.
Choose a type of favored enemy: aberrations, beasts, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, giants, monstrosities, oozes, plants, or undead. Alternatively, you can select two races of humanoid (such as gnolls and orcs) as favored enemies.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them.
When you gain this feature, you also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored enemies, if they speak one at all.
You choose one additional favored enemy, as well as an associated language, at 6th and 14th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of monsters you have encountered on your adventures.

features.name: Natural Explorer (1 terrain type)
features.desc:
You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. Choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, or swamp. When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in.
While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain, you gain the following benefits:
- Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.
- Your group can't become lost except by magical means.
- Even when you are engaged in another activity while traveling (such as foraging, navigating, or tracking), you remain alert to danger.
- If you are traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
- When you forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.
- While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.
You choose additional favored terrain types at 6th and 10th level.

features.name: Fighting Style
features.desc: At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

options.name: Fighting Style: Archery
options.desc: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

options.name: Fighting Style: Defense
options.desc: While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

options.name: Fighting Style: Dueling
options.desc: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

options.name: Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting
options.desc: When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

features.name: Spellcasting: Ranger
features.desc: By the time you reach 2nd level, you have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a druid does.

features.name: Ranger Archetype
features.desc: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate, such as the Hunter. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

features.name: Primeval Awareness
features.desc: Beginning at 3rd level, you can use your action and expend one ranger spell slot to focus your awareness on the region around you. For 1 minute per level of the spell slot you expend, you can sense whether the following types of creatures are present within 1 mile of you (or within up to 6 miles if you are in your favored terrain): aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead. This feature doesn't reveal the creatures' location or number.

features.desc:

In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such those created by the entangle spell.

features.desc:
Starting at 10th level, you can spend 1 minute creating camouflage for yourself. You must have access to fresh mud, dirt, plants, soot, and other naturally occurring materials with which to create your camouflage.
Once you are camouflaged in this way, you can try to hide by pressing yourself up against a solid surface, such as a tree or wall, that is at least as tall and wide as you are. You gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks as long as you remain there without moving or taking actions. Once you move or take an action or a reaction, you must camouflage yourself again to gain this benefit.

features.desc: Starting at 14th level, you can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, you can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.

features.name: Feral Senses
features.desc:
At 18th level, you gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it.
You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.

features.name: Foe Slayer
features.desc: At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your favored enemies. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.

subclasses.name: Hunter
subclasses.desc: Emulating the Hunter archetype means accepting your place as a bulwark between civilization and the terrors of the wilderness. As you walk the Hunter's path, you learn specialized techniques for fighting the threats you face, from rampaging ogres and hordes of orcs to towering giants and terrifying dragons.

features.name: Hunter's Prey
features.desc:
At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Colossus Slayer
Giant Killer
Horde Breaker

options.name: Hunter's Prey: Colossus Slayer
options.desc: Your tenacity can wear down the most potent foes. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, the creature takes an extra 1d8 damage if it's below its hit point maximum. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

options.name: Hunter's Prey: Giant Killer
options.desc: When a Large or larger creature within 5 feet of you hits or misses you with an attack, you can use your reaction to attack that creature immediately after its attack, provided that you can see the creature.

options.name: Hunter's Prey: Horde Breaker
options.desc: Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target and within range of your weapon.

features.name: Defensive Tactics
features.desc:
At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Escape the Horde
Multiattack Defense
Steel Will

options.name: Defensive Tactics: Escape the Horde
options.desc: Opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage.

options.name: Defensive Tactics: Multiattack Defense
options.desc: When a creature hits you with an attack, you gain a +4 bonus to AC against all subsequent attacks made by that creature for the rest of the turn.

options.name: Defensive Tactics: Steel Will
options.desc: You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

features.name: Multiattack
features.desc:
At 11th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Volley
Whirlwind Attack

options.name: Multiattack: Volley
options.desc: You can use your action to make a ranged attack against any number of creatures within 10 feet of a point you can see within your weapon's range. You must have ammunition for each target, as normal, and you make a separate attack roll for each target.

options.name: Multiattack: Whirlwind Attack
options.desc: You can use your action to make a melee attack against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate attack roll for each target.

features.name: Superior Hunter's Defense
features.desc:
At 15th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Evasion
Stand Against the Tide
Uncanny Dodge

options.name: Superior Hunter's Defense: Evasion
options.desc: When you are subjected to an effect, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or a lightning bolt spell, that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

options.name: Superior Hunter's Defense: Stand Against the Tide
options.desc: When a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to repeat the same attack against another creature (other than itself) of your choice.

options.name: Superior Hunter's Defense: Uncanny Dodge
options.desc: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

subclasses.name: Beast Master
subclasses.desc: A ranger bound to a loyal animal partner, the two of them scouting, hunting and fighting as a single, well-drilled team.

features.name: Ranger's Companion
features.desc: You gain a beast companion: a beast no larger than Medium with a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower. Your proficiency bonus is added to its AC, attack rolls and damage rolls, and to any saves and skills it is proficient in. Its hit point maximum is the higher of its normal maximum and four times your ranger level, and like any creature it can spend Hit Dice during a short rest. It shares your initiative count and only takes an action when you command one. On your turn you can tell it where to move (no action needed), and you can use your action to command it to take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge or Help action; once you have Extra Attack, you can also make one weapon attack yourself when you command it to Attack. It uses its reaction (an opportunity attack, say) without waiting for your command. When you are incapacitated or not around, it decides for itself, putting your safety and its own first. When only the two of you are crossing your favored terrain, you can travel stealthily at a normal pace. If it dies, you can bond with a new beast (the same kind or another) that isn't hostile to you by spending 8 hours bonding with it magically.

features.name: Companion Beast
features.desc: Choose your animal companion. The numbers below are the beast's ordinary stat block: add your proficiency bonus to its AC, attack rolls and damage rolls, and its hit point maximum is the higher of the listed value and four times your ranger level. With the DM's agreement you can pick another beast of Medium size or smaller and CR 1/4 or lower.

options.name: Companion: Wolf
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 13, 11 HP (2d8), speed 40 ft. Bite: +4 to hit, 2d4 + 2 piercing, and a creature it hits makes a DC 11 Strength save or is knocked prone. Keen hearing and smell (advantage on Perception that relies on them); Pack Tactics (advantage on attacks when an ally of the wolf is within 5 feet of the target). Perception +3, Stealth +4.

options.name: Companion: Panther
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 12, 13 HP (3d8), speed 50 ft, climb 40 ft. Bite: +4 to hit, 1d6 + 2 piercing. Claw: +4 to hit, 1d4 + 2 slashing. Pounce: if it moves at least 20 feet straight at a creature and then hits with a claw that turn, the target makes a DC 12 Strength save or is knocked prone, and the panther can bite a prone target as a bonus action. Keen smell. Perception +4, Stealth +6.

options.name: Companion: Mastiff
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/8. AC 12, 5 HP (1d8), speed 40 ft. Bite: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 piercing, and a creature it hits makes a DC 11 Strength save or is knocked prone. Keen hearing and smell. Perception +3.

options.name: Companion: Boar
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 11, 11 HP (2d8), speed 40 ft. Tusk: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 slashing. Charge: if it moves at least 20 feet straight at a target and then hits with its tusk that turn, it deals an extra 1d6 slashing and a creature makes a DC 11 Strength save or is knocked prone. Relentless (once per short or long rest): if 7 damage or less would drop it to 0 hit points, it drops to 1 instead.

options.name: Companion: Giant Badger
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 10, 13 HP (2d8), speed 30 ft, burrow 10 ft. Bite: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 piercing. Claws: +3 to hit, 2d4 + 1 slashing. Multiattack (bite and claws) once Bestial Fury lets it use that action. Keen smell, darkvision 30 ft.

options.name: Companion: Giant Weasel
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/8. AC 13, 9 HP (2d8), speed 40 ft. Bite: +5 to hit, 1d4 + 3 piercing. Keen hearing and smell, darkvision 60 ft. Perception +3, Stealth +5.

options.name: Companion: Giant Wolf Spider
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 13, 11 HP (2d8), speed 40 ft, climb 40 ft. Bite: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 piercing, and the target makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 2d6 poison damage on a failure or half on a success; if the poison drops it to 0 hit points, it is stable but poisoned and paralyzed for 1 hour. Climbs walls and ceilings freely, senses creatures touching its web, ignores webbing. Blindsight 10 ft, darkvision 60 ft. Perception +3, Stealth +7.

options.name: Companion: Giant Poisonous Snake
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 14, 11 HP (2d8), speed 30 ft, swim 30 ft. Bite: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft, 1d4 + 4 piercing, and the target makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 3d6 poison damage on a failure or half on a success. Blindsight 10 ft. Perception +2.

options.name: Companion: Giant Crab
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/8. AC 15, 13 HP (3d8), speed 30 ft, swim 30 ft. Claw: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 bludgeoning, and the target is grappled (escape DC 11); it has two claws, each able to grapple one target. Breathes air and water. Blindsight 30 ft. Stealth +4.

options.name: Companion: Giant Frog
options.desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 11, 18 HP (4d8), speed 30 ft, swim 30 ft. Bite: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 piercing, and the target is grappled (escape DC 11) and restrained while grappled; the frog can't bite anyone else meanwhile. Swallow (its own action): a bite against a grappled Small or smaller creature swallows it (blinded, restrained, 2d4 acid at the start of each of the frog's turns). Breathes air and water; standing long jump 20 ft, high jump 10 ft. Darkvision 30 ft. Perception +2, Stealth +3.

options.name: Companion: Flying Snake
options.desc: Tiny beast, CR 1/8. AC 14, 5 HP (2d4), speed 30 ft, fly 60 ft, swim 30 ft. Bite: +6 to hit, 1 piercing plus 3d4 poison. Flyby (no opportunity attacks when it flies out of reach). Blindsight 10 ft.

options.name: Companion: Hawk
options.desc: Tiny beast, CR 0. AC 13, 1 HP (1d4), speed 10 ft, fly 60 ft. Talons: +5 to hit, 1 slashing. Keen sight. Perception +4.

options.name: Companion: Blood Hawk
options.desc: Small beast, CR 1/8. AC 12, 7 HP (2d6), speed 10 ft, fly 60 ft. Beak: +4 to hit, 1d4 + 2 piercing. Keen sight; Pack Tactics (advantage on attacks when an ally of the hawk is within 5 feet of the target). Perception +4.

options.name: Companion: Owl
options.desc: Tiny beast, CR 0. AC 11, 1 HP (1d4), speed 5 ft, fly 60 ft. Talons: +3 to hit, 1 slashing. Flyby (no opportunity attacks when it flies out of reach); keen hearing and sight. Darkvision 120 ft. Perception +3, Stealth +3.

options.name: Companion: Giant Rat
options.desc: Small beast, CR 1/8. AC 12, 7 HP (2d6), speed 30 ft. Bite: +4 to hit, 1d4 + 2 piercing. Keen smell; Pack Tactics (advantage on attacks when an ally of the rat is within 5 feet of the target). Darkvision 60 ft.

features.name: Exceptional Training
features.desc: If your companion doesn't attack on one of your turns, you can spend a bonus action to have it Dash, Disengage, Dodge or Help on its turn. Its attacks now count as magical for getting past resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

features.name: Bestial Fury
features.desc: Your companion now attacks twice when you command it to take the Attack action (or it can use its Multiattack instead, if it has one).

features.name: Share Spells
features.desc: When a spell you cast targets you, you can extend it to your companion as well, provided the beast is within 30 feet of you.

features.name: Expertise
features.desc:
At 1st level, choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves' tools. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.
At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools) to gain this benefit

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.desc:
Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon.
You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't incapacitated, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll.
The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue table.

features.name: Thieves' Cant
features.desc:
During your rogue training you learned thieves' cant, a secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. Only another creature that knows thieves' cant understands such messages. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly.
In addition, you understand a set of secret signs and symbols used to convey short, simple messages, such as whether an area is dangerous or the territory of a thieves' guild, whether loot is nearby, or whether the people in an area are easy marks or will provide a safe house for thieves on the run.

features.name: Cunning Action
features.desc: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

features.name: Roguish Archetype
features.desc: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your rogue abilities, such as Thief. Additional archetypes are available in the original source material. Your archetype choice grants you features at 3rd level and then again at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

features.name: Uncanny Dodge
features.desc: Starting at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

features.name: Evasion
features.desc: Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or an ice storm spell. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

features.desc: Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.

features.name: Slippery Mind
features.desc: By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

features.desc: Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.

features.name: Stroke of Luck
features.desc:
At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Thief
subclasses.desc: You hone your skills in the larcenous arts. Burglars, bandits, cutpurses, and other criminals typically follow this archetype, but so do rogues who prefer to think of themselves as professional treasure seekers, explorers, delvers, and investigators. In addition to improving your agility and stealth, you learn skills useful for delving into ancient ruins, reading unfamiliar languages, and using magic items you normally couldn't employ.

features.name: Fast Hands
features.desc: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.

features.name: Second-Story Work
features.desc:
When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement.
In addition, when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Supreme Sneak
features.desc: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

features.name: Use Magic Device
features.desc: By 13th level, you have learned enough about the workings of magic that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.

features.name: Thief's Reflexes
features.desc: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are surprised.

subclasses.name: Assassin
subclasses.desc: A specialist in disguise, poison and the perfect opening, who ends a fight before the target realises it has begun.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.desc: You become proficient with the disguise kit and the poisoner's kit.

features.name: Assassinate
features.desc: You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn yet in the current combat. Every hit you land on a surprised creature is a critical hit.

features.name: Infiltration Expertise
features.desc:
By spending 7 days and 25 gp you can set up a dependable false identity: a history, a profession and contacts, backed by fitting clothes, official-looking papers and letters of introduction. It has to be a new persona; you can't take over a real person's identity this way.
Whenever you wear that persona as a disguise, other creatures accept you as that person unless something obviously gives you away.

features.name: Impostor
features.desc: After spending at least 3 hours studying a person (listening to them talk, examining their handwriting and watching their mannerisms), you can copy their voice, writing and behaviour flawlessly. Casual observers can't see through it; if a wary creature suspects something is off, you have advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks to keep from being found out.

features.name: Death Strike
features.desc: When you hit a surprised creature with an attack, it makes a Constitution saving throw against DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus. On a failure, the damage of that attack against it is doubled.

subclasses.name: Arcane Trickster
subclasses.desc: A rogue who adds a measure of wizardry to the trade, clouding minds with enchantment and illusion and lifting what fingers can't reach with an unseen hand.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.desc:
You cast spells from the wizard spell list, with Intelligence as your spellcasting ability (spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier; spell attack bonus = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier). You have 1st-level slots from 3rd level, 2nd-level slots from 7th, 3rd-level from 13th and 4th-level from 19th, and you regain expended slots on a long rest.
Cantrips: you know mage hand plus two other wizard cantrips of your choice, and you learn one more wizard cantrip at 10th level.
Spells known: you start with three 1st-level wizard spells and learn more as you gain levels (your sheet shows how many). They must be enchantment or illusion spells, except for one spell of any school you choose at 3rd level and one more each at 8th, 14th and 20th level.
Whenever you gain a rogue level, you can swap one wizard spell you know for another of a level you have slots for. The new spell must be enchantment or illusion, unless it replaces one of your any-school spells.

features.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
features.desc:
When you cast mage hand, you can make the spectral hand invisible, and it can do three extra things: slip an object it holds into a container another creature is wearing or carrying, take an object out of such a container, or use thieves' tools at a distance to pick a lock or disarm a trap.
To do one of these without a creature noticing, win a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check against that creature's Wisdom (Perception) check. You can also control the hand with the bonus action from Cunning Action.

features.name: Magical Ambush
features.desc: If you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, that creature has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell this turn.

features.name: Versatile Trickster
features.desc: As a bonus action, choose a creature within 5 feet of your mage hand's spectral hand. You have advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of the turn.

features.name: Spell Thief
features.desc:
Right after a creature casts a spell that targets you or includes you in its area, you can use your reaction to force it to make a saving throw with its spellcasting ability modifier against your spell save DC. On a failure, the spell has no effect on you, and if it is 1st level or higher and of a level you can cast, you steal it: for the next 8 hours you know the spell (even if it isn't a wizard spell) and can cast it with your own spell slots, and the creature can't cast it until those 8 hours are up.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

info.name: Cantrips
info.desc: At 1st level, you know four cantrips of your choice from the sorcerer spell list. You learn additional sorcerer cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Sorcerer table.

info.name: Spell Slots
info.desc:
The Sorcerer table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these sorcerer spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
For example, if you know the 1st-level spell burning hands and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast burning hands using either slot.

info.name: Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher
info.desc:
You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the sorcerer spell list.
The Spells Known column of the Sorcerer table shows when you learn more sorcerer spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 3rd level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level. 
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the sorcerer spells you know and replace it with another spell from the sorcerer spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

info.name: Spellcasting Ability
info.desc:
Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your sorcerer spells, since the power of your magic relies on your ability to project your will into the world. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a sorcerer spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

info.name: Spellcasting Focus
info.desc: You can use an arcane focus as a spellcasting focus for your sorcerer spells.

features.name: Spellcasting: Sorcerer
features.desc: An event in your past, or in the life of a parent or ancestor, left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with arcane magic. This font of magic, whatever its origin, fuels your spells.

features.name: Sorcerous Origin
features.desc:
Choose a sorcerous origin, which describes the source of your innate magical power, such as Draconic Bloodline.
Your choice grants you features when you choose it at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.

features.name: Font of Magic
features.desc:
At 2nd level, you tap into a deep wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by sorcery points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.
Sorcery Points
You have 2 sorcery points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer table. You can never have more sorcery points than shown on the table for your level. You regain all spent sorcery points when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Flexible Casting: Creating Spell Slots
features.desc:
You can transform unexpended sorcery points into one spell slot as a bonus action on your turn. The Creating Spell Slots table shows the cost of creating a spell slot of a given level. You can create spell slots no higher in level than 5th. 
Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Flexible Casting: Converting Spell Slot
features.desc: As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend one spell slot and gain a number of sorcery points equal to the slot's level..

features.name: Metamagic
features.desc:
At 3rd level, you gain the ability to twist your spells to suit your needs. You gain two of the following Metamagic options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th level.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

options.name: Metamagic: Careful Spell
options.desc: When you cast a spell that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can protect some of those creatures from the spell's full force. To do so, you spend 1 sorcery point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell.

options.name: Metamagic: Distant Spell
options.desc:
When you cast a spell that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can spend 1 sorcery point to double the range of the spell.
When you cast a spell that has a range of touch, you can spend 1 sorcery point to make the range of the spell 30 feet.

options.name: Metamagic: Empowered Spell
options.desc:
When you roll damage for a spell, you can spend 1 sorcery point to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). You must use the new rolls.
You can use Empowered Spell even if you have already used a different Metamagic option during the casting of the spell.

options.name: Metamagic: Extended Spell
options.desc: When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 sorcery point to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.

options.name: Metamagic: Heightened Spell
options.desc: When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, you can spend 3 sorcery points to give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell.

options.name: Metamagic: Quickened Spell
options.desc: When you cast a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 sorcery points to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

options.name: Metamagic: Subtle Spell
options.desc: When you cast a spell, you can spend 1 sorcery point to cast it without any somatic or verbal components.

options.name: Metamagic: Twinned Spell
options.desc:
When you cast a spell that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can spend a number of sorcery points equal to the spell's level to target a second creature in range with the same spell (1 sorcery point if the spell is a cantrip).
To be eligible, a spell must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the spell's current level. For example, magic missile and scorching ray aren't eligible, but ray of frost is.

options.desc: When you cast a spell that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 sorcery point to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.

options.name: Metamagic: Heightened Spell
options.desc: When you cast a spell that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, you can spend 3 sorcery points to give one target of the spell disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the spell.

options.name: Metamagic: Quickened Spell
options.desc: When you cast a spell that has a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 sorcery points to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

options.name: Metamagic: Subtle Spell
options.desc: When you cast a spell, you can spend 1 sorcery point to cast it without any somatic or verbal components.

options.name: Metamagic: Twinned Spell
options.desc:
When you cast a spell that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can spend a number of sorcery points equal to the spell's level to target a second creature in range with the same spell (1 sorcery point if the spell is a cantrip).
To be eligible, a spell must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the spell's current level. For example, magic missile and scorching ray aren't eligible, but ray of frost is.

features.name: Sorcerous Origin feature
features.desc:
Choose a sorcerous origin, which describes the source of your innate magical power, such as Draconic Bloodline.
Your choice grants you features when you choose it at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

features.name: Sorcerous Restoration
features.desc: At 20th level, you regain 4 expended sorcery points whenever you finish a short rest.

subclasses.name: Draconic
subclasses.desc: Your innate magic comes from draconic magic that was mingled with your blood or that of your ancestors. Most often, sorcerers with this origin trace their descent back to a mighty sorcerer of ancient times who made a bargain with a dragon or who might even have claimed a dragon parent. Some of these bloodlines are well established in the world, but most are obscure. Any given sorcerer could be the first of a new bloodline, as a result of a pact or some other exceptional circumstance.

You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.

features.name: Draconic Resilience
features.desc:
As magic flows through your body, it causes physical traits of your dragon ancestors to emerge. At 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class.
Additionally, parts of your skin are covered by a thin sheen of dragon-like scales. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Elemental Affinity
features.desc: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell. At the same time, you can spend 1 sorcery point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.

features.name: Dragon Wings
features.desc:
At 14th level, you gain the ability to sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. You can create these wings as a bonus action on your turn. They last until you dismiss them as a bonus action on your turn.
You can't manifest your wings while wearing armor unless the armor is made to accommodate them, and clothing not made to accommodate your wings might be destroyed when you manifest them.

features.name: Draconic Presence
features.desc: Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the dread presence of your dragon ancestor, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 sorcery points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were casting a concentration spell), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.

subclasses.name: Wild Magic
subclasses.desc: Your power springs from raw, untamed chaos rather than any orderly bloodline, and it does not always do what you ask of it.

features.name: Wild Magic Surge
features.desc:
Your spells can set off bursts of untamed magic. Once per turn, right after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the DM can have you roll a d20. On a 1, roll a d100 on the table below and that effect happens. If the effect is a spell, Metamagic can't change it, and it needs no concentration: it simply lasts its full duration.
Wild Magic Surge table (d100):
01-02: For the next minute, roll on this table at the start of each of your turns (ignore this result if it comes up again during that minute).
03-04: For 1 minute, you can see any invisible creature you have line of sight to.
05-06: A modron appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you; the DM picks and controls it, and it vanishes after 1 minute.
07-08: You cast fireball as a 3rd-level spell, centred on yourself.
09-10: You cast magic missile as a 5th-level spell.
11-12: Roll a d10 and change your height by that many inches: shorter on an odd roll, taller on an even roll.
13-14: You cast confusion, centred on yourself.
15-16: For 1 minute, you regain 5 hit points at the start of each of your turns.
17-18: You sprout a long beard of feathers that stays until you sneeze, when the feathers burst off your face.
19-20: You cast grease, centred on yourself.
21-22: If you cast a spell that calls for a saving throw within the next minute, every save against the first such spell is made with disadvantage.
23-24: Your skin turns a vivid blue; a remove curse spell ends this.
25-26: For 1 minute an extra eye opens on your forehead, giving you advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
27-28: For 1 minute, every spell you cast that normally takes 1 action takes 1 bonus action instead.
29-30: You teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
31-32: You are whisked to the Astral Plane until the end of your next turn, then return to the space you left (or the nearest unoccupied space if it is taken).
33-34: The next damaging spell you cast within 1 minute deals maximum damage.
35-36: Roll a d10 and change your age by that many years: younger on an odd roll (never below 1 year old), older on an even roll.
37-38: 1d6 flumphs appear in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of you, controlled by the DM and frightened of you; they vanish after 1 minute.
39-40: You regain 2d10 hit points.
41-42: You become a potted plant until the start of your next turn: incapacitated and vulnerable to all damage. If you drop to 0 hit points, the pot breaks and you return to your own form.
43-44: For 1 minute, you can teleport up to 20 feet as a bonus action on each of your turns.
45-46: You cast levitate on yourself.
47-48: A unicorn controlled by the DM appears within 5 feet of you and vanishes after 1 minute.
49-50: For 1 minute you can't speak; pink bubbles drift out of your mouth whenever you try.
51-52: For 1 minute a ghostly shield floats beside you, giving you +2 AC and immunity to magic missile.
53-54: For the next 5d6 days, alcohol can't make you drunk.
55-56: All your hair falls out; it grows back within 24 hours.
57-58: For 1 minute, any flammable object you touch catches fire, unless another creature is wearing or carrying it.
59-60: You regain your lowest-level expended spell slot.
61-62: For 1 minute, you can only speak by shouting.
63-64: You cast fog cloud, centred on yourself.
65-66: Up to three creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you take 4d10 lightning damage.
67-68: You are frightened of the nearest creature until the end of your next turn.
69-70: For 1 minute, every creature within 30 feet of you is invisible; a creature's invisibility ends when it attacks or casts a spell.
71-72: For 1 minute, you have resistance to all damage.
73-74: A random creature within 60 feet of you is poisoned for 1d4 hours.
75-76: For 1 minute you shed bright light in a 30-foot radius; any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of you is blinded until the end of its next turn.
77-78: You cast polymorph on yourself; if you fail the saving throw, you become a sheep for the spell's duration.
79-80: For 1 minute, illusory butterflies and flower petals drift through the air within 10 feet of you.
81-82: You can take one extra action right away.
83-84: Each creature within 30 feet of you takes 1d10 necrotic damage, and you regain hit points equal to the total necrotic damage dealt.
85-86: You cast mirror image.
87-88: You cast fly on a random creature within 60 feet of you.
89-90: For 1 minute you are invisible and other creatures can't hear you; the invisibility ends if you attack or cast a spell.
91-92: If you die within the next minute, you come straight back to life as if by the reincarnate spell.
93-94: For 1 minute, you are one size category larger.
95-96: For 1 minute, you and every creature within 30 feet of you have vulnerability to piercing damage.
97-98: For 1 minute, faint otherworldly music plays around you.
99-00: You regain all your expended sorcery points.

features.name: Tides of Chaos
features.desc: You can give yourself advantage on one attack roll, ability check or saving throw. Once you do, you can't do it again until you finish a long rest. Until then, the DM can have you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table right after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher; if that happens, you get this use back.

features.name: Bend Luck
features.desc: When a creature you can see makes an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll a d4 and add it to or subtract it from that roll (your choice). You can do this after the roll but before any of its effects happen.

features.name: Controlled Chaos
features.desc: Whenever you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table, you roll twice and choose which of the two results happens.

features.name: Spell Bombardment
features.desc: Once per turn, when you roll damage for a spell and one or more dice show their highest possible number, pick one of those dice, roll it again and add the new roll to the damage.

info.name: Cantrips
info.desc: You know two cantrips of your choice from the warlock spell list. You learn additional warlock cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Warlock table.

info.name: Spell Slots
info.desc:
The Warlock table shows how many spell slots you have. The table also shows what the level of those slots is; all of your spell slots are the same level. To cast one of your warlock spells of 1st level or higher, you must expend a spell slot. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a short or long rest.
For example, when you are 5th level, you have two 3rd-level spell slots. To cast the 1st-level spell thunderwave, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a 3rd-level spell.

info.name: Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher
info.desc:
At 1st level, you know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the warlock spell list.
The Spells Known column of the Warlock table shows when you learn more warlock spells of your choice of 1st level and higher. 
A spell you choose must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level. When you reach 6th level, for example, you learn a new warlock spell, which can be 1st, 2nd, or 3rd level.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the warlock spells you know and replace it with another spell from the warlock spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

info.name: Spellcasting Ability
info.desc:
Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your warlock spells, so you use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a warlock spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

info.name: Spellcasting Focus
info.desc: You can use an arcane focus as a spellcasting focus for your warlock spells.

features.name: Otherworldly Patron
features.desc: At 1st level, you have struck a bargain with an otherworldly being of your choice, such as the Fiend. Your choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Pact Magic
features.desc: Your arcane research and the magic bestowed on you by your patron have given you facility with spells.

features.name: Eldritch Invocations
features.desc:
In your study of occult lore, you have unearthed eldritch invocations, fragments of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability.
At 2nd level, you gain two eldritch invocations of your choice. Your invocation options are detailed at the end of the class description. When you gain certain warlock levels, you gain additional invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations Known column of the Warlock table.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the invocations you know and replace it with another invocation that you could learn at that level.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Agonizing Blast
options.desc: When you cast eldritch blast, add your Charisma modifier to the damage it deals on a hit.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Armor of Shadows
options.desc: You can cast mage armor on yourself at will, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Beast Speech
options.desc: You can cast speak with animals at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Beguiling Influence
options.desc: You gain proficiency in the Deception and Persuasion skills.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Book of Ancient Secrets
options.desc:
You can now inscribe magical rituals in your Book of Shadows. Choose two 1st-level spells that have the ritual tag from any class's spell list (the two needn't be from the same list). The spells appear in the book and don't count against the number of spells you know. With your Book of Shadows in hand, you can cast the chosen spells as rituals. You can't cast the spells except as rituals, unless you've learned them by some other means. You can also cast a warlock spell you know as a ritual if it has the ritual tag.
On your adventures, you can add other ritual spells to your Book of Shadows. When you find such a spell, you can add it to the book if the spell's level is equal to or less than half your warlock level (rounded up) and if you can spare the time to transcribe the spell. For each level of the spell, the transcription process takes 2 hours and costs 50 gp for the rare inks needed to inscribe it.

options.desc: You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet.

options.desc: You can cast detect magic at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Eldritch Spear
options.desc: When you cast eldritch blast, its range is 300 feet.

options.desc: You can cast false life on yourself at will as a 1st-level spell, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.desc: You can use your action to touch a willing humanoid and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn. While perceiving through the other creature's senses, you benefit from any special senses possessed by that creature, and you are blinded and deafened to your own surroundings.

features.desc: At 3rd level, your otherworldly patron bestows a gift upon you for your loyal service. You gain one of the following features of your choice.

options.name: Pact of the Chain
options.desc:
You learn the find familiar spell and can cast it as a ritual. The spell doesn't count against your number of spells known.
When you cast the spell, you can choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: imp, pseudodragon, quasit, or sprite.
Additionally, when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its reaction.
Your familiar is more cunning than a typical familiar. Its default form can be a reflection of your patron, with imps and quasits tied to the Fiend.

options.name: Pact of the Blade
options.desc:
You can use your action to create a pact weapon in your empty hand. You can choose the form that this melee weapon takes each time you create it. You are proficient with it while you wield it. This weapon counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
Your pact weapon disappears if it is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more. It also disappears if you use this feature again, if you dismiss the weapon (no action required), or if you die.
You can transform one magic weapon into your pact weapon by performing a special ritual while you hold the weapon. You perform the ritual over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a short rest. You can then dismiss the weapon, shunting it into an extradimensional space, and it appears whenever you create your pact weapon thereafter. You can't affect an artifact or a sentient weapon in this way. The weapon ceases being your pact weapon if you die, if you perform the 1-hour ritual on a different weapon, or if you use a 1-hour ritual to break your bond to it. The weapon appears at your feet if it is in the extradimensional space when the bond breaks.
If you serve the Fiend, your weapon could be an axe made of black metal and adorned with decorative flames.

options.desc:

While the book is on your person, you can cast those cantrips at will. They don't count against your number of cantrips known. If they don't appear on the warlock spell list, they are nonetheless warlock spells for you.
If you lose your Book of Shadows, you can perform a 1-hour ceremony to receive a replacement from your patron. This ceremony can be performed during a short or long rest, and it destroys the previous book. The book turns to ash when you die.
Your Book of Shadows could be a weighty tome bound in demon hide studded with iron, holding spells of conjuration and a wealth of forbidden lore about the sinister regions of the cosmos, a gift of the Fiend.

At 11th level, your patron bestows upon you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one 6th- level spell from the warlock spell list as this arcanum.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Armor of Shadows

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Beast Speech

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Beguiling Influence

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Book of Ancient Secrets
options.desc:

The spells appear in the book and don't count against the number of spells you know. With your Book of Shadows in hand, you can cast the chosen spells as rituals. You can't cast the spells except as rituals, unless you've learned them by some other means. You can also cast a warlock spell you know as a ritual if it has the ritual tag.
On your adventures, you can add other ritual spells to your Book of Shadows. When you find such a spell, you can add it to the book if the spell's level is equal to or less than half your warlock level (rounded up) and if you can spare the time to transcribe the spell. For each level of the spell, the transcription process takes 2 hours and costs 50 gp for the rare inks needed to inscribe it.

options.desc: You can cast detect magic at will, without expending a spell slot.

options.desc: When you cast eldritch blast, its range is 300 feet.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Eyes of the Rune Keeper
options.desc: You can read all writing.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Fiendish Vigor
options.desc: You can cast false life on yourself at will as a 1st-level spell, without expending a spell slot or material components.

options.name: Eldritch Invocation: Gaze of Two Minds
options.desc: You can use your action to touch a willing humanoid and perceive through its senses until the end of your next turn. As long as the creature is on the same plane of existence as you, you can use your action on subsequent turns to maintain this connection, extending the duration until the end of your next turn. While perceiving through the other creature's senses, you benefit from any special senses possessed by that creature, and you are blinded and deafened to your own surroundings.

features.name: Eldritch Master
features.desc:
At 20th level, you can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power while entreating your patron to regain expended spell slots. You can spend 1 minute entreating your patron for aid to regain all your expended spell slots from your Pact Magic feature.
Once you regain spell slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

subclasses.name: Fiend
subclasses.desc: You have made a pact with a fiend from the lower planes of existence, a being whose aims are evil, even if you strive against those aims. Such beings desire the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you. Fiends powerful enough to forge a pact include demon lords such as Demogorgon, Orcus, Fraz'Urb-luu, and Baphomet; archdevils such as Asmodeus, Dispater, Mephistopheles, and Belial; pit fiends and balors that are especially mighty; and ultroloths and other lords of the yugoloths.

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
features.desc: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
features.desc:
Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience
features.desc: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silver weapons ignores this resistance.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
features.desc:
Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape.
At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Archfey
subclasses.desc: Your patron is a ruler of the fey, a being of moonlit beauty and fickle moods who repays service with glamour, trickery and the occasional cruel jest.

features.name: Fey Presence
features.desc:
As an action, you let a flash of fey majesty spill out of you: each creature in a 10-foot cube starting from you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Every creature that fails is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Misty Escape
features.desc:
When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You stay invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a spell.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Beguiling Defenses
features.desc: You can't be charmed. When another creature tries to charm you, you can use your reaction to turn the charm back on it: it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

features.name: Dark Delirium
features.desc:
As an action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) for 1 minute or until your concentration breaks (you concentrate as if on a spell); the effect also ends early if the creature takes any damage. While it lasts, the creature believes it is lost in a misty dream-realm whose look you decide, and it can see and hear only itself, you and the illusion.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Great Old One
subclasses.desc: You are bound to something vast and unknowable from beyond the stars or the deep dark, whose thoughts seep into yours as strange insight and quiet dread.

features.name: Awakened Mind
features.desc: You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You don't need a shared language, but the creature has to understand at least one language to follow you.

features.name: Entropic Ward
features.desc:
When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to give that roll disadvantage. If the attack misses, you have advantage on your next attack roll against that creature, as long as you make it before the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Thought Shield
features.desc: Telepathy and other means can't read your thoughts unless you allow it. You have resistance to psychic damage, and whenever a creature deals psychic damage to you, it takes the same amount of damage that you do.

features.name: Create Thrall
features.desc: As an action, you touch an incapacitated humanoid and taint its mind with your patron's alien magic. It is charmed by you until a remove curse spell is cast on it, the charmed condition is removed from it, or you use this feature again. While you and it are on the same plane of existence, you can communicate with it telepathically.

info.name: Cantrips
info.desc: At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. You learn additional wizard cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Wizard table.

info.name: Spellbook
info.desc: At 1st level, you have a spellbook containing six 1st- level wizard spells of your choice. Your spellbook is the repository of the wizard spells you know, except your cantrips, which are fixed in your mind.

info.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
info.desc:
The Wizard table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.
You prepare the list of wizard spells that are available for you to cast. To do so, choose a number of wizard spells from your spellbook equal to your Intelligence modifier + your wizard level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
For example, if you're a 3rd-level wizard, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With an Intelligence of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination, chosen from your spellbook. If you prepare the 1st-level spell magic missile, you can cast it using a 1st-level or a 2nd-level slot. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells.
You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of wizard spells requires time spent studying your spellbook and memorizing the incantations and gestures you must make to cast the spell: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

info.name: Spellcasting Ability
info.desc:
Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your wizard spells, since you learn your spells through dedicated study and memorization. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a wizard spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier.

info.name: Ritual Casting
info.desc: You can cast a wizard spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell in your spellbook. You don't need to have the spell prepared.

info.name: Spellcasting Focus
info.desc: You can use an arcane focus as a spellcasting focus for your wizard spells.

features.name: Spellcasting: Wizard
features.desc: As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.desc:
You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.
For example, if you're a 4th-level wizard, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level spell slot or two 1st-level spell slots.

features.name: Arcane Tradition
features.desc:
When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation.
Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

features.name: Spell Mastery
features.desc:
At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.
By spending 8 hours in study, you can exchange one or both of the spells you chose for different spells of the same levels.

features.name: Spell Mastery (2nd level)
features.desc: Your second mastered spell: a 2nd-level spell from your spellbook that you can cast at its lowest level without a slot, as often as you like, while you have it prepared.
