features.name: Signature Spell
features.desc:
When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

subclasses.name: Evocation
subclasses.desc: You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast enemy armies from afar. Others use their spectacular power to protect the weak, while some seek their own gain as bandits, adventurers, or aspiring tyrants.

features.name: Evocation Savant
features.desc: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.desc: Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.desc: Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
features.desc: Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

features.name: Overchannel
features.desc:
Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.
The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

subclasses.name: Abjuration
subclasses.desc: You study the magic of wards and barriers: shielding allies, banishing intruders and unravelling hostile spells before they land.

features.name: Abjuration Savant
features.desc: The gold and time you spend copying an abjuration spell into your spellbook are halved.

features.name: Arcane Ward
features.desc:
When you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, you can also wrap yourself in a magical ward that lasts until you finish a long rest. You can create the ward only once per long rest.
The ward has a hit point maximum of twice your wizard level + your Intelligence modifier. When you take damage, the ward takes it first; whatever is left after the ward drops to 0 hit points carries over to you. At 0 hit points the ward absorbs nothing, but it still exists, and each time you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher it regains hit points equal to twice the spell's level.

features.name: Projected Ward
features.desc: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to have your Arcane Ward absorb that damage instead. If the ward drops to 0 hit points, the creature takes whatever damage is left.

features.name: Improved Abjuration
features.desc: When an abjuration spell has you make an ability check as part of casting it (counterspell and dispel magic, for example), you add your proficiency bonus to that check.

features.name: Spell Resistance
features.desc: You have advantage on saving throws against spells, and you have resistance to damage from spells.

subclasses.name: Conjuration
subclasses.desc: You pull creatures and objects out of thin air and step from one place to another, mastering the magic of summoning and travel.

features.name: Conjuration Savant
features.desc: The gold and time you spend copying a conjuration spell into your spellbook are halved.

features.name: Minor Conjuration
features.desc: As an action, you create an inanimate, nonmagical object in your hand or in an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of you. It must be something you have seen before, no more than 3 feet on a side and no heavier than 10 pounds. It is obviously magical and sheds dim light within 5 feet. It disappears after 1 hour, when you use this feature again, or as soon as it takes or deals any damage.

features.name: Benign Transposition
features.desc:
As an action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, or trade places with a willing Small or Medium creature within that range.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest or cast a conjuration spell of 1st level or higher.

features.name: Focused Conjuration
features.desc: Taking damage can't break your concentration on a conjuration spell.

features.name: Durable Summons
features.desc: Every creature you summon or create with a conjuration spell has 30 temporary hit points.

subclasses.name: Divination
subclasses.desc: You read omens and glimpse what is hidden or still to come, and fate bends a little toward what you have foreseen.

features.name: Divination Savant
features.desc: The gold and time you spend copying a divination spell into your spellbook are halved.

features.name: Portent
features.desc: Each time you finish a long rest, roll two d20s and note the results: these are your foretelling rolls. You can replace an attack roll, saving throw or ability check made by you or by a creature you can see with one of them. You must decide before the roll is made, you can do this only once per turn, and each foretelling roll can be used only once. Any you haven't used are lost when you finish your next long rest.

features.name: Expert Divination
features.desc: When you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher using a spell slot, you regain one expended spell slot. The regained slot must be of a lower level than the spell you cast, and no higher than 5th level.

features.name: The Third Eye
features.desc:
As an action, you sharpen your senses, choosing one of the benefits below each time you use this feature. It lasts until you are incapacitated or you take a short or long rest, and you can't use the feature again until you finish a short or long rest.
Darkvision: you gain darkvision out to 60 feet.
Ethereal Sight: you can see into the Ethereal Plane within 60 feet of you.
Greater Comprehension: you can read any language.
See Invisibility: you can see invisible creatures and objects within 10 feet of you that are in your line of sight.

features.name: Greater Portent
features.desc: Your Portent now gives you three foretelling rolls (three d20s) after each long rest instead of two.

subclasses.name: Enchantment
subclasses.desc: You master magic that sways minds, turning enemies into friends and friends into followers with a glance and a word.

features.name: Enchantment Savant
features.desc: The gold and time you spend copying an enchantment spell into your spellbook are halved.

features.name: Hypnotic Gaze
features.desc:
As an action, choose a creature you can see within 5 feet of you. If it can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn. While charmed this way, its speed is 0 and it is incapacitated and visibly dazed.
On later turns you can spend your action to extend the effect until the end of your next turn. It ends early if you move more than 5 feet away from the creature, if it can neither see nor hear you, or if it takes damage. Once the effect ends, or if the creature succeeds on its first save, you can't use this feature on that creature again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Instinctive Charm
features.desc: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to try to redirect it, as long as another creature is within the attack's range. You decide before you know whether the attack hits. The attacker makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC; on a failure it must attack the creature closest to it other than you and itself (the attacker picks if several are equally close). On a success, you can't use this feature on that attacker again until you finish a long rest. Creatures that can't be charmed are immune.

features.name: Split Enchantment
features.desc: When you cast an enchantment spell of 1st level or higher that targets only one creature, you can have it target a second creature as well.

features.name: Alter Memories
features.desc: When you cast an enchantment spell that charms one or more creatures, you can make one of them unaware that it is charmed. In addition, once before the spell ends, you can use your action to blur that creature's memory of the time it spent charmed: it makes an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC or forgets up to 1 + your Charisma modifier hours (minimum 1). You may erase less, and never more than the spell's duration.

subclasses.name: Illusion
subclasses.desc: You weave light, sound and suggestion into convincing falsehoods, until the line between what seems and what is wears thin.

features.name: Illusion Savant
features.desc: The gold and time you spend copying an illusion spell into your spellbook are halved.

features.name: Improved Minor Illusion
features.desc: You learn the minor illusion cantrip (if you already know it, you learn another wizard cantrip of your choice instead), and it doesn't count against your cantrips known. When you cast minor illusion, one casting can create both a sound and an image.

features.name: Malleable Illusions
features.desc: While an illusion spell of yours with a duration of 1 minute or longer is active and you can see the illusion, you can use your action to change it, within the spell's normal limits.

features.name: Illusory Self
features.desc:
When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to put an illusory double of yourself in the way. The attack automatically misses you, and the double fades.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Illusory Reality
features.desc: When you cast an illusion spell of 1st level or higher, you can pick one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make it real for 1 minute, using a bonus action on your turn while the spell lasts (an illusory ladder your friends can actually climb, say). The object can't deal damage or directly harm anyone.

subclasses.name: Necromancy
subclasses.desc: You study the forces of life, death and undeath, drawing strength from the fallen and bending the dead to your will.

features.name: Necromancy Savant
features.desc: The gold and time you spend copying a necromancy spell into your spellbook are halved.

features.name: Grim Harvest
features.desc: Once per turn, when a spell of 1st level or higher that you cast kills one or more creatures, you regain hit points equal to twice the spell's level, or three times its level if it is a necromancy spell. Killing constructs or undead gives you nothing.

features.name: Undead Thralls
features.desc:
Animate dead goes into your spellbook if it isn't there already. When you cast it, you can target one extra corpse or pile of bones, raising one more zombie or skeleton.
Every undead you create with a necromancy spell has its hit point maximum increased by your wizard level and adds your proficiency bonus to its weapon damage rolls.

features.name: Inured to Undeath
features.desc: You have resistance to necrotic damage, and your hit point maximum can't be reduced.

features.name: Command Undead
features.desc:
As an action, choose an undead you can see within 60 feet of you. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a success, you can never use this feature on it again. On a failure, it becomes friendly to you and obeys your commands until you use this feature again.
Clever undead resist: one with Intelligence 8 or higher has advantage on the save, and one with Intelligence 12 or higher that fails can repeat the save at the end of every hour until it succeeds and breaks free.

subclasses.name: Transmutation
subclasses.desc: You reshape matter and flesh alike, turning one substance into another and chasing the alchemist's dream of perfect change.

features.name: Transmutation Savant
features.desc: The gold and time you spend copying a transmutation spell into your spellbook are halved.

features.name: Minor Alchemy
features.desc: You can temporarily turn a nonmagical object made entirely of wood, stone (not gemstones), iron, copper or silver into a different one of those materials. Each 10 minutes of work transforms up to 1 cubic foot. The change lasts 1 hour or until your concentration breaks (you concentrate as if on a spell), then the material returns to what it was.

features.name: Transmuter's Stone
features.desc:
Over 8 hours you can craft a transmuter's stone. Whoever carries it (you, or someone you give it to) gains one benefit you choose when you make it:
Darkvision out to 60 feet.
+10 feet of speed while unencumbered.
Proficiency in Constitution saving throws.
Resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage (pick the type each time you choose this benefit).
While the stone is on you, you can switch its benefit each time you cast a transmutation spell of 1st level or higher. If you make a new stone, the old one stops working.

features.name: Shapechanger
features.desc: Polymorph goes into your spellbook if it isn't there already. You can cast it without using a spell slot, but then it can target only you, and you must become a beast of challenge rating 1 or lower. After casting it this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest; you can still cast it normally with a slot.

features.name: Master Transmuter
features.desc:
As an action, you can release all the magic stored in your transmuter's stone at once for one of the effects below. The stone is destroyed, and you can't make a new one until you finish a long rest.
Major Transformation: after 10 minutes of handling a nonmagical object no bigger than a 5-foot cube, you turn it into another nonmagical object of similar size and mass and of equal or lower value.
Panacea: a creature you touch is cured of all curses, diseases and poisons and regains all its hit points.
Restore Life: you cast raise dead on a creature you touch with the stone, without using a spell slot or needing the spell in your spellbook.
Restore Youth: a willing creature you touch with the stone becomes 3d10 years younger in appearance (minimum 13 years old); its lifespan is not extended.
